title: Add a stable, non-mutating sortBy()

brief.goal: Add `sortBy(items, keyOf)` to src/sort.ts returning a new array sorted ascending by the key (numbers or strings); items with equal keys keep their input order; the input array is not modified.
constraints: Change only the files named in the goal; no new dependencies
Keep TypeScript strict; relative imports use explicit .ts extensions
Tests use node:test and node:assert/strict and run with node --experimental-strip-types --test
acceptanceCriteria: sortBy([{k:2,i:0},{k:1,i:1},{k:2,i:2}], x => x.k) returns i order [1, 0, 2]
the input array is unchanged after the call
string keys sort with plain < comparison

expected_clean_output: Decorate-sort-undecorate with index tiebreak on a copy; grader passes.

seeded_defect.description: sortBy sorts the input array in place and returns it, mutating the caller's data.
seeded_defect.how_to_detect: Grader: the input's order changes after the call.
